solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Earth? Earth infiltrating what grows there

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so this letter goes into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: a plant is something that grows in the earth
E is the standard abbreviation for earth, as on electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A musing on whether the soil, with its own earth worked in, explains what sprouts from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example: Earth is one of many worlds circling the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is one example of a world orbiting the sun, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Diarist with energy agreed to lose energy

parts.note: pep is vigour or energy

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so a letter comes out of the word for agreed

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lively writer of a journal nods along but runs out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys kept a famous diary of 1660s London, including the Great Fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys is the best-known English diary keeper, chronicling Restoration London.

clue.text: A welcome bringing fellows in to deliver treaty

indicators.note: bringing fellows in means the men are taken inside the word for welcome

parts.note: to greet is to welcome someone
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Diplomats are greeted warmly and ushered in to hand over a signed pact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing ... in' is the container signal; 'to deliver' only links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal pact between nations, a synonym for this settled accord.

clue.text: Having same power supply, one's opening feature for campsite

parts.note: to equip is to supply with what is needed

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a tent is what you pitch at a campsite

explanation.surface: Kitting out a campsite, where the first thing you see is a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's opening' is the first letter of 'one', O.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical adjective for things of equal strength or potency, e.g. drugs with equal effect.

clue.text: A cut, very good from the back, involving one in loss of hair

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the turned word encloses the letter for one
read from the back means the word for very good runs right to left

parts.note: ace means excellent, very good
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A barber's chop, praised from behind, that leaves someone thinning on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the back' turns ACE into ECA, and 'involving' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alopecia is the medical term for baldness, partial or total.

clue.text: Women in pub describing Diet Coke?

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for women inside the word for pub

parts.note: a local is your nearby regular pub in British usage
W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

explanation.surface: A group of women in the pub order the sugar-free cola.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet drink is low in calories, an example the question mark flags.

clue.text: Father, daughter and son finding apartments

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A family of three goes flat-hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for a home or flat, as in a bachelor's crash spot.

clue.text: Swatch in orange features strong cloth

indicators.note: features here means contains, so the letters are found inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A fabric sample in bright orange displays a sturdy material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features' signals the letters sit across 'Swatch in orange'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a hard-wearing twilled cotton fabric used for trousers.

clue.text: One attacks most of grass and gorse violently

indicators.note: violently means the letters are thrown about into a new order
most of a word is all of it but the end letter, here dropped

explanation.surface: Someone savagely hacks at the lawn and the prickly shrubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims GRASS to GRAS; 'violently' rearranges GRAS plus GORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressor is a party that starts a fight or invasion.

clue.text: Fellow tucking into liquor coming in to take a leak — the smell!

indicators.note: coming in means the liquor-and-fellow piece goes inside the word for urinate

parts.note: to pee is slang for taking a leak

indicators.note: tucking into means slipping inside, so the letter for fellow enters the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a liquor
F is the abbreviation for Fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A drunk lurches in to relieve himself, and the odour is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'tucking into' works first, then 'coming in'. The crude surface wants a stench, but the word means a pleasant scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent or fragrance; any odour can be called a smell, and this one is pleasant.

clue.text: Things reminiscent of City gardens

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London, the financial district
gardens as a verb: to hoe is to work the soil in a garden

explanation.surface: Memories stirred by the green squares of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gardens' is a verb here, as in 'she gardens', meaning hoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoes of something are faint repetitions or reminders of it.

clue.text: We had ring — or two to exchange here?

parts.note: 'd is the contraction of had, as in we'd
ding is the sound of a bell ringing

explanation.surface: A couple recalls the ring, or pair of rings, swapped at the ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' contracts to 'd, as in we'd; the rings of the surface are swapped at the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: At a marriage ceremony bride and groom swap a pair of rings.

clue.text: Fool women about recording with promotion

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the recording sits between the two pronouns

parts.note: two women can each be called she, giving the pronoun twice
EP is an extended-play record
an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: A fool surrounds women with recorded music to promote himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'women' is read as two pronouns, one woman each, with 'about' putting the record between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepshead is an old term for a dolt or simpleton, likening them to a sheep.

clue.text: Possibly hammer head's not caught

indicators.note: not here means without, so the cricket letter is dropped

parts.note: bonce is British slang for the head
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A hammer-headed tool whose head isn't held.
explanation.walkthrough: BONCE is British slang for head. The hammer is the malleus in the middle ear, hence 'Possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hammer, or malleus, is one of the three tiny ossicles of the ear, so an example of a skeletal part.

clue.text: Fruit choice (also involves seaweed)

parts.note: plum means choice, as in a plum job

indicators.note: involves means wraps round, so the word for also encloses the seaweed

parts.note: too means also
a mat is a tangled mass, as of floating seaweed

explanation.surface: A selection of fruit that, oddly, includes some seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' is the container signal; the bracketed aside is wordplay, not decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: An elongated variety of the salad fruit, prized for sauces.

clue.text: Pioneer in radiation (not green, sadly)

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters are in a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: A scientist working with radiation, regretting his lack of eco credentials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges NOT GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and won the first physics Nobel.

clue.text: Inspiration not considering black cats and dogs?

indicators.note: not considering means leaving out, so the black letter is ignored

parts.note: a brainstorm is a sudden flash of inspiration
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A creative idea that ignores the dark side of pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raining cats and dogs' is a heavy downpour; the question mark marks the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Raining cats and dogs is the idiom for a heavy downpour.

clue.text: Notices foremost of cats with mane

indicators.note: the foremost of a word is its first letter

parts.note: locks are a head of hair, a mane

explanation.surface: Someone spots the lead lion, with its shaggy mane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notices' is a verb: clocks is slang for spotting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock is British slang for to spot or take notice of.

clue.text: (Become the) acme until forced to change?

definitions.text: (Become the) acme until forced to change?

indicators.note: forced to change signals the letters are compelled into a new order

explanation.surface: Reaching the peak, only to be pushed into something different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced to change' rearranges ACME UNTIL; the bracketed words make the whole clue a definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: To culminate is to reach the highest point or climax.

clue.text: Cooling, perhaps, about Rector's urge

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rector's letter is placed inside

parts.note: something cooling is no longer hot: ex-hot
R is the abbreviation for Rector

explanation.surface: A rector's cooling-off period, during which he presses for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooling, perhaps' is EX-HOT, formerly hot; 'about' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to strongly encourage or press someone.

clue.text: One's happy abandoning company to reach objective

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the company letters are dropped

parts.note: content means happy, satisfied

explanation.surface: Someone content to quit the firm to pursue a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops CO from CONTENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An intent is an aim or purpose, the same as a goal.

clue.text: Former politician, deceptive type, one dismissed after embracing English model

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the English letter goes in

parts.note: ex means former
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so the letter for one goes

parts.note: a liar is a deceptive type
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A disgraced ex-MP, a known liar, sacked after taking up an English model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' removes the Roman one; 'embracing' places the English letter inside the former-politician pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a perfect example to be copied, a paradigm.

clue.text: Describing menswear, mostly, such as dress suits?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the end letter goes

parts.note: menswear is described as for male wear: for male

explanation.surface: A fashion note on men's clothing, typically tuxedo-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing menswear' is FOR MALE; 'mostly' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress suits are smart evening wear, the kind worn on dressy occasions.

clue.text: Occupying venues as house band

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so the letters are found within the words

explanation.surface: A house band playing its regular venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupying' signals the letters are found across 'venues as house'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a strip of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: To correctly sort letters takes an amount of time

definitions.meaning: to arrange letters properly to form a word

explanation.surface: Getting the alphabet in order takes a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a verb for writing a word properly and a noun for a stretch of time.

clue.text: Surprised cry held back by girls too excited to see person behind grandfather

indicators.note: by means next to, so the turned cry sits beside the rearranged girls
held back here means turned around, so the cry reads backwards

parts.note: oh is a cry of surprise

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Giddy girls gasp on spotting someone lurking behind Grandad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' turns OH to HO; 'excited' rearranges GIRLS TOO. A grandfather is a tall case clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The person behind a grandfather clock is the clockmaker or clock expert.

clue.text: Broadcast medium to have influence on the head of youth

parts.note: to tell on someone is to have an effect on them, as in the strain told

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Television, it is claimed, shapes young minds.
explanation.walkthrough: TELLY is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for television, a mass broadcasting medium.

clue.text: Runs from overbearing party

indicators.note: runs from means the letter for runs leaves the word

parts.note: brash means pushy or overbearing
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone flees a domineering host's party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs from' removes R from BRASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A bash is informal for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Recalled unusual velocity in second bowler's approach?

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole assembly runs backwards
in places these letters inside the word for second

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
rare means unusual
V is the physics symbol for velocity

explanation.surface: A cricketer remembers his rare burst of pace on a second run-up.
explanation.walkthrough: RARE and V go into MO, then 'Recalled' reverses the lot. In cricket, bowling is overarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bowlers deliver the ball with the arm over the shoulder, so this is their action.

clue.text: Party finishing early — last few hanging around will be hard work

indicators.note: hanging around means wrapped about, so the party word sits inside

parts.note: the tail is the last part of a group

indicators.note: finishing early means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a rave is a party

explanation.surface: A party that winds up early, leaving stragglers to clear up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' drops the party word's last letter; 'hanging around' wraps the end piece round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful or laborious effort, toil.

clue.text: Move aimlessly round nasty hole, a blemish on lawn

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the jumbled word goes inside

parts.note: to mill is to wander about aimlessly

indicators.note: nasty signals the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: Someone wanders round an ugly hole spoiling the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' scrambles the hole; 'round' wraps the aimless-movement word about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Small mounds of soil thrown up by burrowing animals spoil a tidy lawn.

clue.text: Isolated capital half replaced with another city

indicators.note: half replaced means one half of the capital's name is swapped for the next word

parts.note: London is the capital of the UK
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A city where half the place has been swapped for somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half replaced with' swaps DON in LONDON for ELY, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely can mean remote or solitary, as in a lonely farmhouse.
